JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act 1989, claiming compensation amount of Rs.1,85,00,000/- with costs and interest from date of accident till date of realization, in respect of death of Sri.Ravi P., who succumbed to injuries on 25.06.2024 in Road Traffic Accident.
2. The brief facts of the petitioner are summarized as under:
On 25.06.2024 at about 4.25 p.m., the deceased Ravi.P., was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-H-8091 on Malavalli-Kollegala Road.
Due to heavy rain the said deceased was unable to proceed in the said motor cycle near Kanagal Halla and therefore deceased stood beneath a tree along with his vehicle.
At that time, the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 10-F-0514 came in rash and negligent manner from Malavalli and dashed the deceased.
Due to the impact of accident, the deceased fell down and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
3. Immediately after the accident the deceased was shifted to Malavalli Govt. Hospital wherein postmortem was conducted.
The petitioners have incurred a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards transportation of body, funeral, hospitalization and other expenses.
4. Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased Ravi.P., was very hale and healthy and was aged about 43 years and he was working as a Junior Engineer at Shivanasamudra(Blump).
He was earning sum of Rs.1,04,000/- per month from said avocation and he used to contribute all his earnings towards maintenance of his family.
Due to sudden death of deceased, the petitioners have suffered mental shock and agony and their lives have came to stand still.

The petitioner No.1 is wife of the deceased and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the son and daughter of the deceased and they have lost love and affection of the deceased and their lives have became miserable and hence this petition.
5. The accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent drive of the respondent, who drove his vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0514.
The respondent is the owner of the vehicle involved in the accident and accident has taken place due to the negligent drive of the offender bus driver.

Hence Shivamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84620399/
2
the respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore the petitioner prays to award compensation of Rs.1,85,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till the realization.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
6. After registration of the petition, notice was issued against respondent.
In pursuance of service of notice the respondent has appeared through its counsel and has filed its written statement on behalf of respondent by denying the entire petition averments.
Further denied the expenses incurred for funeral ceremony.
Further denied the age of the deceased, avocation and income of the said deceased.
Further denied the other contents of the petition.
The compensation has claimed by the petitioners are highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
7. In order to substantiate the claim petition, the 1 st petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18.
The respondent has examined its Conductor as RW.1 and no documents were marked on its behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials available on record.

9. Upon considering rival contentions raised by the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Ravi.P., died in the Motor vehicle accident that occurred on 25.06.2024 at about 3.30 p.m., near Kanagal Halls Shiramahalli Cross, Malavalli Kollegal road, N.G. Doddi, Mandya, due to the rash and negligence driving of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0514 by its driver?
2.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
10. My findings on the above issues are as under.
Issue No.1:

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative.

Issue No.3: Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.4: As per the final orders for  the following:-

11.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 25.06.2024 at about 4.25 p.m., the deceased Ravi.P., was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-H- 8091 on Malavalli-Kollegala Shivamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84620399/

Due to heavy rain the said deceased was unable to proceed in the said motor cycle near Kanagal Halla and therefore deceased stood beneath a tree along with his vehicle.
At that time, the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0514 came in rash and negligent manner from Malavalli and dashed the deceased.
Due to the impact of accident, the deceased fell down and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
12. To substantiate the petition averments, petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 18 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18.
Ex . P.1
FIR with complaint which reveals that the petitioner No.1 has lodged complaint on 25.06.2024 against the driver of the respondent offender vehicle i.e., KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0514.
Upon the complaint, the police have registered FIR for the offence punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.2 is the crime detail form with sketch which speaks about the occurrence of accident.
Ex.P.3 is the Vehicle seizure mahazar.
The Ex.P.5 is the Inquest report which clearly discloses that, Ravi.P., has died on 25.06.2024 in a Road Traffic Accident.
Ex.P.6 is the IMV report.
Ex.P.7 is the PM report which reveals that, deceased has succumbed to the injuries in the said accident.

Ex.P.8 is the charge sheet which reveals that, police have investigated the matter and filed charge sheet against the driver of the offender vehicle i.e., KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0514.
13.
The Respondent has examined its Conductor as RW.1 by name Sri Basanagouda Biradar.
The said RW.1 has deposed that he is working as KSRTC bus conductor and conversant with the facts of this case.

On 25.06.2024 the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-10-F-0514 was proceeding from Bengaluru towards Chamarajanagar via Malvalli, slowly carefully on the left side of the road and when he reached near Marehalli Kanagal Shivramalli Road, during that time there was heavy rain road was filled by water during that time, the driver tried to stop the bus by applying the break but even with best efforts not to control over the bus due to failure of break in the left side of the road and touched to one person standing along with his two wheeler below the tree due to rain fall.
Due to impact, the person fell down on the road and he died on the spot.
The said person may avoid the accident after seeing front bright light of the bus, he may change the place nearby available space near the tree.
This accident was occurred due to mechanical defect which is not intentional one.
The alleged accident has occurred due to the sole contributory negligent act of the deceased person.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
14. RW.1 was subjected to cross-examination by learned counsel for the petitioner.
During the course of cross-examination RW.1 has admitted that the driver of the offender bus was driving his vehicle between 40 to 50 speed in a heavy rain.
Due to heavy rain the driver of the said offender bus could have stopped his bus till the slow down of the rain and then would have driven his vehicle.
As the driver of the offender bus has to reach the next stop in time, the said offender driver has driven his vehicle in a speed manner.
The accident spot consist of 100 feet road and the driver would have taken every measure to avoid the accident.
15. Per contra, the evidence of PW.1 clearly reveals that the accident has took place by the fault of the offender vehicle driver i.e., RW.1.
During the course of further cross-examination of PW.1 nothing was elicited from the mouth of PW.1, so as to disbelieve his version.

Hence, this court is of the view that the petitioner has proved that due to the rash and negligent driver of the KSRTC driver Shivamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84620399/

sentences.text: 16. Therefore, it is apparent on the face of records that, the respondent has admitted the occurrence of accident and death of deceased has caused due to the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0514.
In the absence of any cogent materials from the respondents in this regard.
The only inference which has to be drawn is that, the accident in question was the result of the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-10-F-0514.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 17.
The PW.1 in her evidence has deposed that, her deceased husband Ravi P., was working as Junior Engineer at Shivanasamudra (Blump) and was earning Rs.1,04,000/- per month.
Her husband was aged about 43 years and was hale and healthy before the occurrence of accident.
Petitioners being wife, son and daughter of the deceased Ravi.P., were wholly dependent on the income of the said deceased, he being a sole bread earning member in his family.
She has further deposed that, she has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards funeral and other expenses.

Petitioners have averred in the petition that, the petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased Ravi.P.,
Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the son and daughter of the said deceased.
To substantiate the same, PW.1 has produced notarized copies of Aadhar cards along with originals of herself, petitioner No.2 and 3.
These documents reflects the relationship of deceased with the petitioners.
The oral and documentary evidence led by PW.1 reflects that, petitioners are the LR's of deceased Ravi P.

Since,
the respondents have not contested the said matter in the evidence led by PW.1.
Then the evidence of PW.1 stands unshaken and the same is sufficient to show that petitioners are the LR's of deceased.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 In the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
18.

Basically three facts lead to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death as per Sarla Verma Case i.e., (i) age of deceased,
(ii) Income of deceased and (iii) Number of dependents.
(i) Age of deceased:
According to the petitioners the age of the deceased at the time of the accident was 43 years.
As per the Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.12, wherein the year of birth of the deceased mentioned as 1980, the accident was occurred on 25.06.2024.
So, as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged 44 years.
(ii).Income of the deceased:
According to the petitioners deceased Ravi.P., was working as Junior Engineer at Shivanasamudra (Blump) and was earning Rs.1,04,000/- per month.

In this regard, the petitioner has produced Original salary certificate, Bank statement and account statement of the deceased which are marked at Ex.P.9, 10 and Ex.P.18.

As per Ex.P.9 is the salary certificate in which May-2024 gross salary of the deceased Rs.1,04,159/-,
Income tax of Rs.7,000/- and Professional tax Rs.200/- is to be deducted.
Hence, the actual salary of the deceased Rs.96,959/- per month.
19. Loss of dependency:
The following issues are to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at loss of dependency, they are (i) addition/deduction to be made for arriving at the income.
(ii) Deductions to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased.
(iii) The multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.

20. As per the decision reported in National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "if the deceased is below 40 years 40% of the established income of deceased towards future prospectus; an addition of 25%
where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years; an addition 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the same formula to the case on hand it is clear that, the deceased is entitled for future prospects.
In the present case the deceased is aged between 40 to 50 years and therefore 25% of the established income of the deceased is assessed towards future prospects.
Hence, the future prospects is determined as Rs.24,239/- (96,959 X 25/100 = Rs.24,239/-).

Therefore the total income of the deceased is determined as Rs.1,21,198/- per month ( 96,959 + 24,239 =
Rs.1,21,198/-).
21.
Admittedly, petitioner No.1 to 3 are the dependents of deceased person.

As per the the Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298 case, when there are 2 to 3 Dependants 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.

sentences.text:
As such 1/3rd amount is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses i.e.,
Rs.40,399/-.
When the said 1/3rd amount is deducted from monthly income of the deceased, then the balance amount shall be Rs.80,799/- (Rs.1,21,198 - Rs.40,399 = Rs.80,799/-).

As per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd.,
and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier to the age of the deceased is 14.

Hence, Loss of dependency is determined as Rs.1,35,74,232/-.
22.

Transportation, Funeral expenses, Loss of Estate, Loss of love and affection and Loss of Consortium:- In so far as the funeral and other expenses are concerned, as per the version of the petitioners they have spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
But they have not produced any documents to substantiate the said version.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sheti and other the Compensation under the heads of transportation, funeral expenses, loss of estate, loss of love and affection and loss of consortium has to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/- i.e.,
(15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Further, for funeral expenses of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/-
i.e., (15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Like wise
for loss of estate to the extent of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% every three years.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/- i.e., (15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Similarly, for loss of love and affection to the extent of Rs.25,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% every three years.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.27,500/- i.e., (25,000 X 10/100 =Rs.2,500/- + Rs.25,000/-).
Loss of consortium:
it is pertinent to note that, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi case has directed to award an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards consortium.

Subsequently, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 has held that, the term "consortium" is compendious of spousal, parental and filial consortium and directed to award amount in all three categories.

24. Admittedly, the respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,

ISSUE NO.4:-

25. For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.1,37,83,232/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 50:25:25.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of awarded amount of petitioner No.1, 60% shall be released to petitioner No.1 on her proper identification and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in her name in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
The entire amount awarded to the petitioners No.2 and 3, shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in their names in any Scheduled Bank, till they attain the age of majority.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
